title: India's Cricket Tour of Bangladesh Faces Yet Another Postponement Threat
excerpt: A scheduling clash with the newly announced India-Afghanistan T20I series and unresolved diplomatic tensions cast doubt over the twice-deferred September tour.
body:
• India's white-ball tour of Bangladesh, rescheduled to September 2026, faces fresh uncertainty after the BCCI announced a three-match T20I series against Afghanistan in Delhi on September 13, 15, and 17 — directly overlapping with the Bangladesh window.
  • The tour was originally set for August 2025 but was postponed to September 2026 amid diplomatic tensions and security concerns following Bangladesh's political upheaval in 2024.
  • The BCB says it remains confident of hosting India, with the team scheduled to arrive August 28 for three ODIs and three T20Is running through September 13.
  • BCCI officials have remained non-committal about the tour, and the Indian government's approval is reportedly still pending.

India's twice-postponed white-ball tour of Bangladesh is in jeopardy once more. The Board of Control for Cricket in India's announcement of a three-match T20I series against Afghanistan in Delhi — scheduled for September 13, 15, and 17 — has thrown a fresh wrench into plans for the Bangladesh visit, which was set to run through September 13 in the same window.

It marks the latest twist in a saga that has been entangled with deteriorating diplomatic relations between New Delhi and Dhaka for over a year.

A Tour That Keeps Slipping

India was originally supposed to tour Bangladesh for three ODIs and three T20Is in August 2025. That plan collapsed amid the political upheaval that followed the student movement in July 2024, which ousted the Awami League government led by Sheikh Hasina. Security concerns and a sharp deterioration in bilateral ties made the tour untenable.

https://x.com/ProteasMenCSA/status/2090743343873491173

In a joint statement last July, the BCCI and Bangladesh Cricket Board agreed to defer the series to September 2026. The BCB subsequently announced revised dates: the Indian team would arrive on August 28, with ODIs on September 1, 3, and 6, and T20Is on September 9, 12, and 13, according to Cricbuzz.

Bangladesh even postponed its own tour of Ireland to accommodate the India series in that September window.

The Afghanistan Overlap

The BCCI's August 12 announcement of the Afghanistan T20I series created an immediate scheduling conflict. With India-Afghanistan matches set for September 13, 15, and 17, India cannot realistically complete both tours without compressing its squad rotation or pulling out of one.

The overlap is not accidental in the eyes of observers. "The scheduling of the Afghanistan T20I series in Delhi during the same window has added another complication to India's proposed Bangladesh tour," The Business Standard reported from Dhaka. The move has been interpreted in Bangladesh as a signal that the BCCI may be looking for an exit.

Diplomatic Fault Lines Persist

Cricket between the two countries has become a proxy for broader political tensions. The crisis deepened after Bangladesh boycotted its World Cup matches in India, a response to Kolkata Knight Riders dropping Bangladesh pacer Mustafizur Rahman from the IPL. Hopes briefly revived when Bangladesh's new BNP government took power in February following parliamentary elections.

"We are confident about hosting India as per schedule. Everyone is well aware about the benefits of playing a white-ball series against a top side like India and the signs are positive."

— Asif Rabbani, BCB media committee chairman

But those hopes dimmed on August 5, when ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina held a press conference in India, further straining relations between Dhaka and New Delhi. Recent Indian media reports suggest the BCCI is waiting for the Indian government's explicit approval before committing to the tour.

The BCB's Optimism — and Financial Stakes

Despite the uncertainty, the BCB has pressed ahead. It floated Expressions of Interest for media rights covering its 2026 and 2027 home internationals, specifically mentioning India's tour — a move that signals confidence, or at least determination.

The financial stakes are enormous. An India tour is the BCB's single most valuable commercial property. The board had paused its media rights sale process earlier when the tour's status was unclear, and has since restarted it on the assumption India will arrive.

Bangladesh has also taken encouragement from India's June 28 resumption of tourist visa processing for Bangladeshi nationals, the first time in two years, and from public statements by Bangladesh's new Sports Minister Aminul Haque expressing hope of mending sporting ties.

What Happens Now

The ball is firmly in the BCCI's court. If the tour proceeds, some schedule adjustment would be needed to avoid the Afghanistan overlap — likely pushing the final T20I dates or truncating the Bangladesh series. If it doesn't, it would mark the second consecutive year India has pulled out, dealing a financial and reputational blow to the BCB.

For fans of both teams, the uncertainty has become exhausting. The series was meant to be a step toward normalizing sporting relations. Instead, it has become a barometer of just how fraught those relations remain.
nri_angle: The India-Bangladesh cricket dispute reflects broader South Asian diplomatic rifts that affect diaspora communities on both sides, particularly the large Bangladeshi population in the UK and Indian fans who follow the bilateral rivalry.
